title: All 4 API endpoints are unauthenticated — no access control anywhere
evidence: POST /api/analyze accepts any JSON body from any caller. GET /api/roast, /api/compare, /api/persona all return data without any auth check. No middleware.ts exists. No API keys, no CORS origin check, no header validation anywhere.
rationale: In a hackathon demo, this is expected — no real user data is at risk and all data is pre-cached. In production, every endpoint would need auth. Severity downgraded to P2 because this is a demo with mock data.
fix_guidance: For production: add Next.js middleware with API key validation or JWT bearer token. For demo: document that endpoints are intentionally open for easy evaluation.

title: Anonymous users can reach server_internal functions through unauthenticated endpoints
evidence: POST /api/analyze calls loadAllDemoData() which reads filesystem caches. Client-side code cannot directly import server-only modules (checked — 'use client' boundaries prevent direct imports), but any caller can trigger server functions through the unauthenticated API. This is the intended architecture — the API IS the boundary.
rationale: Boundary exists (API routes are server-only, client can't import cache.ts directly). But since the boundary has no auth, it's effectively transparent. Low risk for demo since data is public mock data.
fix_guidance: Acceptable for hackathon demo. Add rate limiting to prevent abuse. Add origin check for production.

title: DEMO_MODE env var used as sole branching mechanism — no origin/header differentiation
evidence: Route branches on `process.env.DEMO_MODE === 'true' || cacheExists()`. No differentiation based on request origin, user-agent, or headers. Same response regardless of who calls.
rationale: Trivial for a demo. The single branching mechanism (demo vs live) is clear and intentional.
fix_guidance: No fix needed for demo. Production would need proper auth middleware before the branch.

title: Demo mode is permanent once cache files exist — no reversible toggle
evidence: cacheExists() checks `fs.existsSync(path.join(CACHE_DIR, 'wallet-a-ethereum.json'))`. If DEMO_MODE=false but cache files exist, `|| cacheExists()` still activates demo mode. Setting env var to 'false' is ignored.
rationale: The `|| cacheExists()` fallback is a deliberate convenience — if cache data exists, use it. This is by design for the demo. Not a security issue since there's no sensitive data.
fix_guidance: If strict env var control is needed: remove `|| cacheExists()` and only check DEMO_MODE env var. Otherwise, accept this as intentional convenience.

title: Phase transitions bypassable via React DevTools — setPhase reachable from browser
evidence: `setPhase` is React state setter in a 'use client' component. Four setTimeout chains (2s/20s/58s/76s) auto-advance phases. React DevTools can directly call setPhase('cta') to skip the entire flow and reach the payment mock. Demo launch (launchDemo) is module-level constant, callable from console.
rationale: This is inherent to client-side React state machines. A user pressing 'cta' early sees the payment button but has no real data (battleData/compareData = null). Low impact — the demo still works, just with empty state.
fix_guidance: For demo: acceptable. For production: move phase sequencing server-side with SSE push, or validate server-side that prerequisites were met before returning data for each phase.
